A_target.statement:
In [[Definition:System F|System F]], let $\mathsf {Nat} = \forall \alpha. \paren {\alpha \to \alpha} \to \alpha \to \alpha$ and $\bar n = \Lambda \alpha. \lambda f. \lambda x. f^n x$.
Then $\mathsf {zero} = \bar 0$ and $\mathsf {succ} = \lambda n. \Lambda \alpha. \lambda f. \lambda x. f \paren {n \, \alpha \, f \, x}$ satisfy $\mathsf {succ} \, \bar n \twoheadrightarrow_\beta \overline {n + 1}$, and iteration $\mathsf {it}_C \, z \, s \, n = n \, C \, s \, z$ satisfies:
:$\mathsf {it}_C \, z \, s \, \bar 0 \twoheadrightarrow_\beta z, \quad \mathsf {it}_C \, z \, s \, \paren {\mathsf {succ} \, \bar n} \twoheadrightarrow_\beta s \paren {\mathsf {it}_C \, z \, s \, \bar n}$

B_source.statement: For every set $C$, $z \in C$ and $s: C \to C$ there is a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] $h: \N \to C$ with $\map h 0 = z$ and $\map h {n + 1} = \map s {\map h n}$.

substitutions.a natural number n: its own iterator, the map (s, z) -> s^n(z)

object_map.reformulation: Represent each number by the iteration it performs, quantifying over all types to play the role of all sets.

validity_conditions: Impredicative quantification lets a numeral be applied at the type Nat itself, which is used for addition and multiplication.
Only iteration is directly available; predecessor is definable but inefficient, and there is no internal induction principle.
proof_plan: Represent $n$ by the iterator $\bar n$, which sends $s$ and $z$ to $s^n z$ at any type $\alpha$.

By $\beta$-reduction, $\bar 0 \, C \, s \, z \twoheadrightarrow_\beta z$ and $\paren {\mathsf {succ} \, \bar n} \, C \, s \, z \twoheadrightarrow_\beta s \paren {\bar n \, C \, s \, z}$, which are the equations of the source result.
